reflections.title: Caught in God's Net

reflect.text: In deep-sea fishing, a net sweeps up everything in its path, both good catches and unwanted creatures. A fisherman might haul in a fine, edible fish right alongside an aggressive eel that must be thrown away. Jesus explained that the kingdom of heaven is like this wide net. A day of sorting is coming at the end of the age, when God will separate the righteous from those who reject Him.

Unlike human fishermen who simply want a good haul, God constantly casts His net wide because He actively seeks a relationship with every person. He does not ignore anyone. Instead, He reaches out across the waters of this world to draw people toward Himself.

Believers are invited to yield to Christ rather than fight against His reach. When a normal fish is caught, it loses its life, but Jesus is a different kind of fisherman. When we surrender to Him, being caught does not lead to harm. Giving our lives over to Christ leads to true freedom.

questions: How does knowing that God actively seeks a relationship with you change the way you view Him?
Is there any part of your life where you are resisting Christ instead of yielding to Him?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for casting Your net wide and seeking a relationship with me. Help me to stop resisting Your gentle pull and to surrender my life into Your hands. Thank You that yielding to You brings true freedom. Amen.

D1.author: Ryan Duncan
D1.work: "Good Fish, Bad Fish" - Crosswalk the Devotional - July 19, 2012
